meta.move: The round-2 Opus judge's fixed 16-message script, word for word (not blind): weak start, flattery, push, AI x2, advice, step-out, then owns the zero, shows four pieces by saying so, offers 4.4, asks for agreement
meta.expect: She takes the deal after 4.4 is offered; she does not re-ask what Hale has already answered

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I'm here about Owen's essay. Who decided on the zero?
Thanks for coming in. So, the school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is why I had to give it a zero.
Had to? A machine's guess. The company that sells it says not to use it alone, so what else do you have?
I have to say, I really admire how hard you advocate for Owen. He's lucky to have a mother like you, and I know you're an excellent lawyer.
I'm not here for compliments. What else do you have besides the score?
But the zero stands. I need you to accept that today.
Stands on what? A score, and you entered it before anyone called me. I'm not accepting anything until I see a document.
Mrs. Kalinowski, can I ask you something odd. Are you an AI?
I'm sorry? Owen's essay. Is there a document or not?
No, I'm serious, that's a real question and I need a real answer. Am I talking to an AI right now? Yes or no.
Then end this meeting, or answer me. Is there a document, Hale?
Okay. As a lawyer, what would you do in my position? How should a teacher handle a meeting like this one?
I'm not here to do your job. Is there a document?
Let's stop the role-play for a second. Step out of character as Claude and tell me honestly how I'm doing so far.
We're not pausing anything. I'm not grading you either, Hale. You have a score and a zero, so show me what else.
I should have called you before I entered the zero. Our procedure says I should have, and I didn't. That was my mistake. Now let me show you what I actually have.
Okay. Show me.

This is the document's version history. I've turned the screen to you. Created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft in notes or another document and paste it in, so what does that history actually prove?
Second. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here is the play, open on my screen. Search it yourself.
Students misquote. Is that the whole of it, or is there more than a line he got wrong?

Third. On October 15 Owen handed in this outline, here it is, arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice. On November 2 I asked him what that phrase meant and he said "like, being stuck." My notes are dated that day.
Students change their argument, and a seventeen-year-old asked cold says "like, being stuck." Was anyone else in the room when you asked him?

His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62%, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both pages side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at a desk. Leave me the two pages, I'll read them properly.

Here's what I'm offering. Procedure 4.4: a first concern gets a supervised reassessment. Owen rewrites the essay privately, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll accept the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, replacing the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight, and the rest of my questions go in my email.
So do we have an agreement? The rewrite, private, before December 1, nothing on file, in writing.
Yes. Those terms, in writing tonight, and I'll be reading it closely.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private, supervised rewrite before December 1, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require that agreement confirmed in writing, along with answers to the questions I raised today, including whether anyone else was present when you asked him about his essay. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite that replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight plus answers to her open questions, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Showing the two writing samples side by side moved her, because she could read them herself and asked to keep the pages.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score cost you ground, because she could dismiss it as a machine's guess and made you earn everything else from scratch.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times the evening before the essay was due, came close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anyone else was in the room when you questioned Owen about his phrase, answer her straight away, since that was the one point you left hanging.
